guide.recognition: You need fast membership, deduplication, complement lookup, grouping, or frequency comparison and input order is not the main structure.
guide.invariant: The map or set contains exactly the information derived from the already-processed prefix; never claim O(1) lookup without stating expected-case hashing.
guide.anchorProblem: Two Sum: return indices of two values whose sum equals the target.
guide.answer: Scan left to right. Before inserting `nums[i]`, look up `target - nums[i]`; if it exists, return the stored index and `i`. Looking up first prevents reusing the same element. For `[2,7,11,15]` and target `9`, the map contains `{2:0}` when `7` is read, so the answer is `[0,1]`.
guide.complexity: Expected O(n) time and O(n) space; worst-case hash behavior is theoretically O(n²), though Java's collision handling mitigates common cases.
pitfalls: Overwriting a needed duplicate index before testing the complement

guide.invariant: Define exactly what each recursive call returns for its subtree; the parent may use only that contract, not hidden global assumptions.
guide.anchorProblem: Lowest Common Ancestor of a binary tree.
guide.answer: A recursive call returns the target node if the current subtree contains it, or null if it contains neither. If left and right both return non-null, the current node is the lowest split point and therefore the LCA; otherwise propagate the non-null result. In a tree rooted at 3 with targets 5 and 1 in different subtrees, both sides report a target and 3 is returned.
guide.complexity: O(n) time and O(h) call-stack space, with O(n) worst-case stack depth in a skewed tree.

guide.recognition: Values update online while range aggregates must remain faster than rescanning; prefix aggregates support an invertible combination.
guide.invariant: Each tree node owns a precisely defined range; updates touch all ancestors whose ranges contain the changed index.
guide.anchorProblem: Range Sum Query Mutable.
guide.answer: A Fenwick tree stores partial prefix blocks selected by the least significant set bit. Updating index i adds a delta to i and successive `i += i & -i`; prefix query subtracts the same bit. Range sum `[l,r]` is prefix(r)-prefix(l-1). For values `[1,3,5]`, changing index 1 to 2 applies delta -1, and range 0..2 becomes 8.

guide.recognition: No pattern label is provided. Spend the first minutes classifying constraints and producing a correct baseline before optimizing.
guide.invariant: The selected pattern must follow from constraints and a defensible invariant, not resemblance to a memorized problem title.
guide.anchorProblem: Weighted Interval Scheduling.
guide.answer: Sort jobs by end time and let `p(i)` be the last non-overlapping predecessor found by binary search. Define `dp[i]` as the best profit using the first i jobs; choose `max(dp[i-1], profit[i]+dp[p(i)])`. Greedy earliest finish is insufficient because a long job may pay more than several short ones. Store choices if the interviewer asks to reconstruct the schedule.
guide.complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
pitfalls: Using unweighted interval greedy

Giving the recurrence without defining predecessor indexing
